{"id":"JMAP-tjvm.18","title":"/set and /copy methods take untyped create: Option<serde_json::Value> — asymmetric with typed update parameter","description":"Five methods take create as a raw serde_json::Value:

  email.rs:106    email_set(create: Option<serde_json::Value>, update: Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>, ...)
  email.rs:211    email_copy(params: EmailCopyParams, create: serde_json::Value)
  email.rs:252    email_import(emails: &HashMap<String, EmailImportInput<'_>>, ...)    ← this one IS typed
  mailbox.rs:84   mailbox_set(create: Option<serde_json::Value>, ...)
  identity.rs:79  identity_set(create: Option<serde_json::Value>, ...)
  submission.rs:162  email_submission_set(create: Option<serde_json::Value>, ...)

Note the asymmetry: `update` is typed `Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>` and benefits from PatchObject's JSON Pointer key contract. `create` is `serde_json::Value`. The same Email/Mailbox/Identity/EmailSubmission types from jmap_mail_types could be used directly with serde_json::to_value, but the public API forces callers to hand-build raw JSON.

Defensive-code-forcing consequence: every caller writes the same boilerplate:

    let create = serde_json::json!({
        "draft1": {
            "mailboxIds": { "mb-drafts": true },
            "keywords": { "$draft": true },
            "from": [{ "email": "me@example.com" }],
            // ...
        }
    });

with no compile-time check that "mailboxIds" is the right key (RFC 8621 uses camelCase but caller might type snake_case), that the keywords map structure is correct, that the from address shape matches RFC 8621 §4.1.3, etc. The Email type in jmap_mail_types already encodes all of these as typed fields.

Why this is hard to fix: the create body in JMAP /set is "implementation-defined plus the spec-defined typed fields" — server-specific extensions and "create only" fields like mailbox-ids-as-set vs. mailbox-ids-as-array may appear. Email has fields populated by the SERVER (id, blobId, threadId, size, receivedAt) and cannot be passed by the caller.

Three options:

  (a) Type the create param as `Option<HashMap<String, jmap_mail_types::Email>>`. Problems: Email has server-set required fields that the caller doesn't have at create time. Would need an `EmailCreate` view-type (similar to ChatCreate / MailboxCreate patterns in some implementations).

  (b) Type the create param as `Option<HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>>` (still untyped per-entry, but at least the outer map is typed). Marginal improvement; doesn't fix the per-entry typing.

  (c) Accept the trade-off and document explicitly that `create` is intentionally untyped because RFC 8621 §4.1 splits Email fields into "server-set vs client-set" and the typed Email struct does not distinguish. Add a doc-comment warning to each method.

Recommendation: (c) for 0.1.x. File a follow-up bead for the 1.0 cut to design EmailCreate / MailboxCreate / IdentityCreate / EmailSubmissionCreate view-types that omit server-set fields.

Propagation: same finding applies to the six sibling extension-client crates (chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing). Likely all of them have the same untyped-create pattern. Canonical-template sweep candidate.

Mark says NO HUMAN — I have a clear recommendation: option (c) now, file a 1.0 design bead for view-types.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-15T01:52:16Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-15T01:52:16Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-14T18:52:15Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
